The first term is 128 and the common ratio is $\dfrac{192}{128}=\dfrac{3}{2}$.

Suppose there are $k$ terms, so $T_k=972$. Using $T_n=ar^{n-1}$:

$972=128\times\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{k-1}$

$\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{k-1}=\dfrac{243}{32}=\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^5$

$k-1=5$, so $k=6$.

There are 6 terms in the geometric sequence.

$f'(x)=(x-2)2x+(x^2+1)\times1=3x^2-4x+1$, $f''(x)=6x-4$

Stationary points: $3x^2-4x+1=0$, $(3x-1)(x-1)=0$, so $x=\dfrac13$ or $x=1$.

When $x=\dfrac13$, $y=-\dfrac{50}{27}$; when $x=1$, $y=-2$.

Stationary points $\left(\dfrac13,-\dfrac{50}{27}\right)$ and $(1,-2)$.

At $\left(\dfrac13,-\dfrac{50}{27}\right)$: $f''=6\times\dfrac13-4=-2<0$, maximum.

At $(1,-2)$: $f''=6\times1-4=2>0$, minimum.
